I found no per-workflow concurrency setting in the results. The limits are set per account, and only the instance creation rate has a per-workflow component.

- **Concurrency is an account-wide cap.** The official changelog from April 15, 2026 gives the concurrent-instance limit as 50,000, up from 10,000. The instance creation rate is 300 per second per account, with a limit of 100 per second per workflow.
- **Waiting instances don't count.** Per the limits reference, instances that are sleeping via step.sleep, waiting for a retry, or waiting for an event via step.waitForEvent do not count towards concurrency limits.
- **Queueing.** Once active instances hit the cap, an instance that has been in a waiting state will be queued instead of resuming immediately. The changelog lists queued instances per Workflow at 2 million.
- **Higher limits.** If your application requires a higher limit, fill out the Limit Increase Request Form or contact your account team.

Source discrepancies: a third-party AI news site reports the ceiling rising from 4,500 to 50,000. That conflicts with Cloudflare's own changelog, which shows 10,000 as the prior limit. I'd trust the official changelog and limits page. The results don't say when the Workflows v2 rewrite the news site mentions took effect.

content.text:
Cloudflare Workflows doesn't seem to have a per-workflow concurrency setting. I didn't find one in the docs or changelog. The only cap is account-wide: as of April 2026, 50,000 instances can run at once (up from 10,000), and you can ask Cloudflare to raise it with the Limit Increase Request Form. Instances that are sleeping, waiting to retry, or waiting with `step.waitForEvent` don't count toward that limit. Once you hit it, extra instances are queued (up to 2 million per workflow) rather than rejected.

To set your own lower cap, you have to limit how fast instances get created. Two common ways (these are my suggestions, not documented Cloudflare features):

- **Durable Object counter:** before calling `env.MY_WORKFLOW.create()`, take a slot from a counter in a Durable Object. Have the workflow give the slot back in its last step, or in a try/finally.
- **Cloudflare Queue:** send work to a Queue first, and have the consumer only create a new instance when the number of running ones is under your limit. It can check this with `instance.status()`. Otherwise it retries the message later.

Sources:
- [Workflows limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/reference/limits)
- [Changelog: Workflows limits raised (2026-04-15)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-04-15-workflows-limits-raised/index.md)
- [Changelog: Workflows concurrency increased (2025-02-25)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2025-02-25-workflows-concurrency-increased)
